name: Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa
short_description: Renaissance beachfront resort on Ko Samui's Laem Nan peninsula near Lamai Beach, known for private pool villas, two pools and the Quan Spa.
ai_summary: The Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa is an upscale Marriott Bonvoy beachfront property perched on the Laem Nan peninsula at the southern end of Lamai Beach, on Ko Samui's southeast coast. Independent reviewers describe a low-density, village-like layout of walled gardens and private villas, many with plunge pools, four-poster beds draped in mosquito netting and generous open-plan living space. Guests consistently praise the warm, attentive Thai service, strong elite recognition for Bonvoy members (breakfast and villa upgrades reported), a small but scenic boulder-framed beach with good sunset views, and the tranquil setting. Dining draws favourable notes across Banana Leaf (all-day and buffet), the seafood-focused tawaNN and beachside barbecues, with breakfast singled out for quality and variety. The Quan Spa, a 50-metre lap pool and a beachfront pool round out the facilities. Watch-outs recur in the coverage: the property shows its age in places, with dated in-room technology (few bedside outlets, no master switch), villa furniture wear, mosquitoes near plunge pools, a large tidal range that limits swimming for much of the day, and a second pool that feels underused. Limited shuttle service is also noted. Overall it reads as a relaxed, characterful villa resort that trades polish for privacy and hospitality.

Facilities include Quan Spa, a 50-metre lap pool and a separate beachfront pool

Rooms and some furnishings feel dated, so travellers wanting a brand-new, high-tech resort may be disappointed

faqs.question: Where is Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa located?
faqs.answer: It sits on the Laem Nan peninsula at the southern end of Lamai Beach on Ko Samui's southeast coast, in Tambon Maret. The main Lamai strip is a short walk or drive, and Samui International Airport is roughly a 30-minute, about 22-kilometre transfer to the northeast.

faqs.question: What are the rooms and villas like?
faqs.answer: Accommodation ranges from deluxe rooms, some with private whirlpools, to spacious villas of roughly 130 to 215 square metres. Many villas feature private plunge pools, four-poster beds with mosquito netting, open-plan living areas and garden or beachfront settings, though reviewers note the decor and technology feel somewhat dated.

faqs.question: Is the beach good for swimming?
faqs.answer: The resort has a small, scenic beach framed by boulders with excellent sunset views, but reviewers repeatedly note a large tidal range that leaves the water shallow for much of the day. Two swimming pools, including a 50-metre lap pool and a beachfront pool, provide reliable alternatives for swimming.

reviews.title: Review: Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa
reviews.author: Rhys Jones
reviews.summary: Praises the village-like villa layout, superior beach and attentive staff; flags dated tech (few bedside outlets), mosquitoes by plunge pools and an underused second pool.

reviews.title: Review: Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa | Marriott Bonvoy
reviews.author: Etienne Werbinski
reviews.summary: Rates it 8/10 for tranquil setting, attentive service and strong breakfast; notes some villa furniture wear, tide-dependent beach and limited once-daily shuttle. Good villa point value for elites.

reviews.title: Review: Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa, Thailand
reviews.author: Jared Ruttenberg
reviews.summary: Glowing account of a pool villa, Thai hospitality and standout Massaman curry at Banana Leaf; highlights the 50-metre pool, Quan Spa and a favourite granite rock with sunset views.
